task: r6t1 - layout-layer feasibility: can one offset constant separate the pin number from the net label?
mode: read-only. No document write, no canvas write, no save. The only file written is this JSON.

reasons: no single offset constant exists in the repo, so premise (1) of the task fails on the facts
the pin number y is owned by the vendor symbol (hardcoded, orientation-dependent: deltas -4/-5/0/+0.5), so changing it is a symbol rebuild
the only in-repo lever for the flag name is the flag component position, which is the "thirteen edits" case the standing rules already reject
a symbol-level edit would change all 70 pin-number attributes on this page (45 visible) and any other project bound to the same library symbol
verdict.whatWouldWork: if the host ever gains a symbol-level lever, the safe window is a uniform lift of 4.37-5.82 units (measured: below 4.37 the number stays inside the label, above 5.82 it reaches the previous row ink that ends at 784.48)
verdict.doNot: do not edit the library symbol in place, do not rebuild the symbol, do not move 12+ flags one by one, do not shrink the font (already no-go at 3.81/2.85)

answers.one: No such shared constant exists. The pin number y comes from the vendor symbol document; the flag name y comes from the flag component position computed in layout.ts. They are not the same lever, so changing one cannot fix both.
answers.two: Not configurable. There is no y-offset parameter: the only in-repo knobs are the flag component position and netLabelFontSize (font size only). The pin number offset is hardcoded in the library symbol.

twoOffset.premiseCorrection: the task states "any non-zero offset separates them" - that is false: the two ink boxes share their top edge (790.30), so a small shift leaves them overlapping

up.meaning: lift "31" until its bottom clears the label top, before it reaches the row above

down.meaning: push "31" below the label bottom, before it reaches the next row

answers.three: A symbol-level change would move all 70 pin-number attributes at once (45 of them visible; one edit, but in the library, and for every project using C23922). The flag route instead moves 12 of the 14 flag names individually (the "thirteen edits" case), and each move drags its stub and wire with it.
answers.four: There is no constant to restore. Rolling back a library-symbol edit means restoring the vendor symbol document, which this repo does not own; a project-local copy may be created and the original museum copy is not addressable from here. That is a symbol rebuild - high risk.

arithmetic.note: the -0.91498 offset holds for all horizontal pins; the name-to-number delta is NOT a single value (-4 / -5 / 0 / +0.5 appear), so there is no one constant that covers every pin
